# Extended emulator vs Google Cloud Spanner emulator

This fork extends Google's emulator so developers can keep local state, test
backup and recovery workflows, exercise database-role permissions, and run more
of their application's SQL and graph logic before connecting to Cloud Spanner.
It retains the familiar Spanner APIs, client configuration and two SQL dialects.

Jump to the [checklist metrics](#checklist-metrics) or the
[individual-feature scorecard](#individual-feature-scorecard).

## Comparison baseline

Reviewed **2026-10-20** against fork commit `aa2520bf` on
`jay-spanner-extended`. Documentation-only reconciliation followed that commit.

- **Detailed upstream baseline:** [v1.5.58, commit a081a7e7][upstream], the
  upstream commit merged into this fork by `90f17557`. Its commit date is
  2026-09-14; the release was published on 2026-09-15.
- **Newer upstream release:** [v1.5.59][new-release], released 2026-10-14, is
  not merged. The detailed table compares with v1.5.58, not an unversioned
  `latest` image. v1.5.59 adds queue execution/DDL, expression indexes,
  multi-key vector indexes, JSON changes and other fixes. It also adds placement
  metadata views, so those views alone are not an exclusive fork benefit.
- **Evidence:** upstream statements below come from the pinned README and source;
  fork statements link to implementation and representative tests in this checkout.
  Test links show coverage exists, not a fresh passing run. No side-by-side runtime
  benchmark or container comparison was performed for this document.

Google's [current emulator guide][google-guide] was also checked on 2026-10-20.
It documents in-memory state, empty query plans, absent role enforcement and
ignored drop protection. Use the pinned sources for version-specific details.

## Side-by-side behavior and developer value

| Area | Google emulator v1.5.58 | This fork | Developer value and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| State across restarts | In-memory only; state is discarded on exit. [Upstream limitations][upstream-limits] | Optional `--data_dir` persists supported rows, schema, sequences and admin state. Sessions and open transactions remain transient. | Keep fixtures and development databases between runs. [Storage implementation](../backend/storage/persistent_storage.cc), [tests](../backend/storage/persistent_storage_test.cc), [persistence guide](persistence.md). |
| Backup and restore | Backup APIs unsupported. [Upstream limitations][upstream-limits] | Local create, copy, list, update, delete and restore, historical `version_time`, and scheduled backups. Requires `--data_dir`; every backup is physically a full copy. | Test backup tooling and restore workflows locally. [Handlers](../frontend/handlers/backups.cc), [tests](../frontend/handlers/backups_test.cc), [limits](persistence.md#backups). |
| Database roles and privileges | Role and grant DDL is parsed without applying privileges. [Schema updater][upstream-schema] | Roles, grants and memberships in both dialects; sessions with `creator_role` enforce supported object privileges. IAM authentication and authorization remain absent. | Exercise restricted application roles, grants and DEFINER/INVOKER views. [Privilege validator](../backend/query/privilege_validator.cc), [conformance tests](../tests/conformance/cases/fine_grained_access_control.cc). |
| IAM policy API workflows | IAM APIs unsupported. [Upstream limitations][upstream-limits] | Policy storage, retrieval, etags and persistence. Policies are not enforced; `TestIamPermissions` returns requested permissions. | Test policy-management API plumbing; this cannot validate cloud IAM access decisions. [Handlers](../frontend/handlers/policies.cc), [tests](../frontend/handlers/policies_test.cc). |
| Concurrent transactions | One read-write transaction or schema change at a time; competing transactions abort. [Upstream limitations][upstream-limits] | Overlapping transactions, wound-wait lock handling and configurable lock waits; snapshot behavior for `REPEATABLE_READ`. Retries are still required. | Exercise contention, retries and snapshot conflicts locally. [Lock manager](../backend/locking/manager.cc), [lock tests](../backend/locking/manager_test.cc), [transaction tests](../backend/transaction/read_write_transaction_test.cc). |
| `PLAN` / `PROFILE` | No query plan returned; `PROFILE` provides basic execution information. [Upstream limitations][upstream-limits] | Plan trees and local execution statistics, including measured table scans. | Test tools that consume plan and profile responses. Plans and timings do not predict production optimization. [Builder](../backend/query/plan/query_plan_builder.cc), [conformance tests](../tests/conformance/cases/query_modes.cc). |
| `SPANNER_SYS` | Many runtime statistics tables are unavailable. [Upstream limitations][upstream-limits] | Measured query, read, transaction and lock statistics, activity views, TTL and split-point metadata; supported statistics persist with `--data_dir`. | Develop statistics queries and diagnostics without a cloud instance. Physical metrics and some tables remain absent or empty. [Collector](../backend/stats/system_stats_collector.cc), [tests](../tests/conformance/cases/spanner_sys.cc), [table coverage](capabilities.md#queries-and-functions). |
| Graph algorithms | Parsing and validation; algorithms return empty results. [Upstream features][upstream-features] | Computes 13 algorithms, including PageRank, centrality, clustering, similarity and shortest paths; supported `EXPORT DATA` writes results to tables. GoogleSQL only. | Test result-consuming graph workflows. Some methods are emulator-defined; export to CSV/Parquet/Avro discards results. [Implementation](../backend/query/graph/graph_algorithms.cc), [conformance tests](../tests/conformance/cases/graph_algorithms.cc). |
| TTL row deletion | Stores and validates row deletion policy DDL; no fork sweeper. [Schema updater][upstream-schema] | Background sweeper deletes expired rows and generates tagged change-stream records. | Test expiry handling and TTL-driven change consumers. Timing differs from production. [Sweeper](../backend/database/row_deletion_policy_sweeper.cc), [tests](../backend/database/row_deletion_policy_sweeper_test.cc). |
| Restart-safe change streams | Streams exist, but all state is in memory. [Upstream limitations][upstream-limits] | Persists definitions, records and partition history with `--data_dir`; implements resume tokens and fixes update-mutation and child-partition handling. | Restart the emulator and resume supported change consumption. Partition distribution remains simulated. [Handlers](../frontend/handlers/change_streams.cc), [tests](../frontend/handlers/change_streams_test.cc), [guide](change-streams.md). |
| Database drop protection | Accepted but ignored, as documented in the [Google guide][google-guide]. | Enforces drop protection, including database deletion through instance deletion. | Test safeguards in admin tooling. [Handlers](../frontend/handlers/databases.cc), [database tests](../frontend/handlers/databases_test.cc), [instance tests](../frontend/handlers/instances_test.cc). |
| Geo-partitioning | Basic placement DDL; incomplete mutation/alter behavior. [Pinned parser](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/a081a7e71aba5f4d05fc8c6b21ef1a269dcbac28/backend/schema/parser/ddl_parser.jj) | Placement lifecycle and placement keys in both dialects, partition checks and configurable preview DML restrictions. All data remains local. | Test schema and application validation around placement keys. No regional routing or latency simulation. [Detailed differences](placements.md), [conformance tests](../tests/conformance/cases/placements.cc). |

## SQL functions and correctness improvements

The fork inherits most SQL support from upstream. The examples below identify
specific additions or fixes; they are not a count of all supported functions.

| Function area | Google emulator v1.5.58 | This fork and evidence | Developer value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| String and compression | No fork execution replacements for base32/Zstd; `SPLIT_SUBSTR` is absent from the allowlist. [Catalog][upstream-catalog], [allowlist][upstream-functions] | Adds `TO_BASE32` / `FROM_BASE32` and `ZSTD_*` execution, allowlists `SPLIT_SUBSTR`, enables `LCASE` / `UCASE` / `ADDDATE` / `SUBDATE` aliases. [Functions](../backend/query/spanner_string_functions.cc), [query tests](../tests/conformance/cases/query.cc), [engine tests](../backend/query/query_engine_test.cc). | Run encoding, compression and string SQL used by applications. |
| Full-text options | Several parameters are accepted without effect; documented HTML and scoring limitations. [Upstream limitations][upstream-limits] | Extends HTML handling, Unicode/RQUERY parsing, diacritic behavior and scoring options. [Tokenizer](../backend/query/search/tokenizer.cc), [tests](../backend/query/search/tokenizer_test.cc), [scoring tests](../backend/query/search/score_evaluator_test.cc). | Test more search preprocessing and result-handling logic; scores remain local rather than production relevance values. |
| `SNIPPET` response | Uses `start_position` / `end_position` highlight keys. [Evaluator][upstream-snippet] | Uses documented `begin` / `end` string offsets and adds source bounds. [Evaluator](../backend/query/search/snippet_evaluator.cc), [tests](../backend/query/search/snippet_evaluator_test.cc). | Test code that consumes the documented snippet JSON shape. |
| PostgreSQL floating aggregates | Empty/all-NULL floating `SUM` / `AVG` cases are disabled in upstream tests because of result-type failures. [Upstream tests][upstream-pg-tests] | Enables these cases with typed NULL results. [Conformance tests](../tests/conformance/cases/pg_functions_test.cc). | Exercise aggregate edge cases without changing application SQL. |

For the broader function surface and per-feature evidence, use
[Capabilities](capabilities.md#queries-and-functions) and the
[generated feature matrix](feature-coverage.md). Its summary counts feature-area
records, including inherited functionality; it does not measure added functions
or complete production parity.

The [individual-feature scorecard](#individual-feature-scorecard) below expands
these areas into a ✓ / ✗ checklist with generated totals.

## Shared functionality and limits

Both emulators support GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects, Spanner client libraries,
gRPC and REST, and PostgreSQL connections through PGAdapter. Upstream already
provides GQL, change streams, search, indexes and much of the admin API; their
mere presence is not a fork differentiator. Both support x86/arm64 usage.
[Upstream features and installation][upstream]

The fork remains a local development emulator. It does not provide distributed
replication, regional placement, production performance, TLS, authenticated IAM
decisions or production monitoring. Approximate vector functions use exact
results. Persistent non-NULL `PROTO` / `ENUM` values remain unsupported, and row
writes are not synced against host power loss. Queue support in this checkout is
partial; v1.5.59 adds upstream queue execution. Consult [Known gaps](known-gaps.md)
before choosing a feature for a demo.

## Qualification and use in a showcase

The links above are source and representative-test evidence. Historical native
and local Docker results, their dates and changes made afterward are centralized
in [Testing](TESTING.md#qualification-evidence). They do not qualify a current
registry tag, both image architectures or LocalCloud integration.

For a reproducible demo, build the chosen fork revision with `./build.sh` and
record the resulting image identity. Use upstream image tag `1.5.58` for this
table's baseline. Run the selected workflow against both images before claiming
a measured behavioral difference. Update the upstream column if using v1.5.59
or a later release.

<!-- individual-feature-matrix:start -->
## Individual-feature scorecard

This checklist contains **783 individual checks**, covers all **158 canonical inventory records**, and lists every registered RPC and every public name in the GoogleSQL allowlist separately. Bundled inventory records are expanded into operations, types, functions and behaviors. Headings only help navigation; each table row is counted separately.

These are source-reviewed local capabilities at the pinned versions above, not benchmark results or a fresh test run. A check mark applies only to the behavior named in its row; consult the linked inventory notes for limits. Function rows cover the named function, not every overload, input or error. Test links are representative leads from the parent inventory record, not a claim that each individual row has a dedicated passing test. PostgreSQL examples and named options are expanded where tracked; this is not an exhaustive SQL grammar or PostgreSQL function census.

| Symbol | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ✓ | Implemented |
| ✗ | Unavailable |
| ◐ | Partial |
| ○ | Accepted without the described effect |
| — | Not applicable |
| ? | Not established by this source review |

| Status | Google v1.5.58 | Extended |

| ✓ Implemented | 497 | 725 |
| ✗ Unavailable | 164 | 10 |

| ○ Accepted without the described effect | 69 | 34 |
| — Not applicable | 12 | 12 |
| ? Not established by this source review | 0 | 0 |
| **Total individual checks** | **783** | **783** |

**189 checks add implemented behavior** where the upstream baseline is unavailable or has no effect; **39 more expand partial behavior**. Counts describe this checklist only. They are not a production-parity percentage, and splitting a feature into more rows does not make it more important. Shared features are counted in both columns.
